conventions.convention: The site set is Γ = Z^d with finite d ≥ 1, the spin dimension is a positive integer q ≥ 1, and finite regions include the empty set. The empty-region Hilbert space is C.
Configuration-space inner products are linear in the first argument. Local algebras use composition, Hilbert adjoint, the induced operator norm, and the unnormalized finite trace.
Factor inclusions are the canonical configuration-restriction identifications followed by T ↦ T ⊗ I; these identifications allow regrouping of lexicographically ordered sites.
The quasi-local algebra is the norm completion of the directed local algebra, with Countable Choice assumed for completion. No infinite tensor-product Hilbert space is selected.

An algebraic state is a bounded complex-linear functional with ω(I) = 1 and ω(A* A) ≥ 0. Local densities are positive trace-one matrices; consistency uses the unnormalized configuration-basis partial trace.
State convergence means convergence of functional values on every fixed observable, rather than convergence of global density matrices.
The GNS quotient pairing is ⟨[a],[b]⟩ = ω(b* a), consistent with the linear-first convention; cyclicity means norm density of {π(A)Ω : A ∈ A}.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the Cauchy-sequence completion. The local normed *-algebra and its completion are well defined; the completion is a unital complex C*-algebra with norm-dense local algebra. Operators in disjoint finite local regions commute.
For d ≥ 1, q ≥ 1 and finite Λ ⊆ Λ′, the factor inclusion T ↦ T ⊗ I is an isometric unital *-homomorphism. For Λ ⊆ Λ′ ⊆ Λ″, the inclusions compose.

Assume Countable Choice for the norm completion. Every family of positive trace-one finite-region matrices satisfying all partial-trace consistency equations determines a unique infinite algebraic state with those local trace pairings.

For Γ = Z^d and q ≥ 1, the local algebra on finite Λ is B(HΛ), where HΛ consists of complex functions on {1,…,q}^Λ with its configuration inner product; inclusions tensor with the complementary identity.
For every positive integer d, the integer lattice Γ = Z^d is at most countable.

Under Countable Choice and the stated completion and finite positive-square-root interfaces, a consistent local density family and its extended state admit a cyclic unital *-representation with a unit vector Ω satisfying ω(A) = ⟨π(A)Ω,Ω⟩.
